extracted.intended_audience: readers and media professionals interested in AI, journalism, and publishing practices (including SEO and editorial staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A news article summarizing CNET's updated AI content policy, the editorial response to errors in AI-generated drafts, and the implications for publishers and search rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No story will be entirely produced by an AI tool
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET updates its AI policy, stating that no story will be entirely produced by an AI tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humans must remain responsible for final stories; full end-to-end AI authorship is disallowed under the new policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human hands-on review and product testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans will conduct hands-on reviews and testing of products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For product coverage, editorial staff must personally test products rather than relying solely on AI-generated content or summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted AI uses: analysis, outlines, explanatory content
rubrics_metrics.description: The site is exploring the use of AI tools to analyze data, create outlines and generate explanatory content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may assist in research and drafting tasks (data analysis, outlines, explanatory passages) but not replace human authorship or final editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a centralized in-house tool (Responsible AI Machine Partner — RAMP) under editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: The in-house tool is called Responsible AI Machine Partner (RAMP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CNET/its owner is developing and deploying a standardized internal AI tool across brands; centralized tools should be subject to the publisher's editorial oversight and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough editorial review and expansion of AI drafts before publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors first created drafts using AI, then edited and expanded them before publishing, and later reviewed all published AI articles after errors were discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-originated drafts require careful human editing; failure to thoroughly review can produce glaring factual errors (as occurred in 41 of 77 articles reviewed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about AI use and clearer attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET promises more transparency; AI-generated articles were initially published under 'CNET Money Staff' which was later changed to 'CNET Money'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should clearly disclose when AI contributed to content and avoid publishing AI texts 'quietly' without clear attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved plagiarism checks and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET also promises more transparency and better plagiarism checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated content workflows must include robust plagiarism detection and other controls to prevent recycled or unoriginal material from being published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resume AI-assisted publishing only after confidence in editorial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the AI tool will resume once editors are confident that editorial processes are preventing human and AI errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reintroduction of automation should be contingent on demonstrated reliability of editorial safeguards and error prevention measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and fact-checking are critical, especially for personal finance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AI-generated financial articles contained glaring errors; this is especially bad because personal finance articles often include ads for financial products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High factual accuracy is essential where errors can harm readers or interact with monetized product recommendations; extra scrutiny is required for finance reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing AI content that functions as 'AI spam'—prioritize usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Google focuses on 'useful content' rather than how a piece of content is created; treating AI-generated text like spam was previously announced but Google's emphasis is on usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid search devaluation and being labeled as spam, automated content must serve reader utility and not be produced solely for search-engine rankings; publishers must balance automation with quality to prevent devaluation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated insertion of current numeric data must be managed
rubrics_metrics.description: Red Ventures developed a text tool that automatically inserts current numbers, such as interest rates, into financial articles; that tool will remain in operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated updates of dynamic data are permissible but should be governed by editorial controls to ensure correctness and prevent misleading figures.
